company_name: Tiangong International Company Limited (天工國际)
overview: Tiangong International is a Jiangsu, China-based manufacturer of specialty steel and advanced materials, producing die/mould steel (DS), high-speed steel (HSS), HSS and carbide cutting tools, and titanium alloy products. The Group is vertically integrated from raw alloy steel production through to finished cutting tools, and sells both domestically within China and to export markets in Europe and North America. Its titanium alloy business is carried out through majority-owned (67.63% per Group disclosure; some filings cite ~74%) subsidiary Jiangsu Tiangong Technology Co., Ltd. ("TG Tech"), which was spun off and separately listed on the Beijing Stock Exchange (stock code 920068) in May 2025.

business_model.summary: Tiangong manufactures and sells specialty steel products (die steel and high-speed steel) made from alloyed raw materials (molybdenum, chromium, vanadium, tungsten, cobalt), which are either sold as raw steel or further processed into cutting tools and titanium alloy products. Revenue is transactional/order-based (not subscription), driven by sales volume and average selling price (ASP), with the Group generally able to pass through raw material cost increases to customers in strong demand periods (pricing power from "supply loyalty" relationships), compressing margins when it cannot. A small "Others" segment packages/exports hardware and power tool kits.
business_model.customer_type: B2B industrial manufacturers — automotive (incl. NEV die-casting), home appliances, electronics, machinery, aerospace, consumer electronics (titanium alloy frames/hinges), medical devices, and DIY/power-tool retail (export)
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2025 DS: 45.4% domestic / 54.6% export; HSS: 73.0% domestic / 27.0% export; cutting tools: 43.3% domestic / 56.7% export; titanium alloy: 99.3% domestic / 0.7% export. Overall skew toward China domestic demand with meaningful export exposure (especially cutting tools and historically HSS) to Europe and North America.

main_competitors: China Yongbao / other domestic HSS and tool-steel producers
Global titanium alloy/powder producers (for TG Tech's titanium segment) and aluminum alloy as a substitute material in consumer electronics
competitive_position.market_position: Historically the largest integrated HSS and HSS cutting-tool manufacturer in China by volume/revenue (per older filings, ~44.7% domestic HSS market share circa IPO-era disclosures; current share not independently verified in this review). The Group is positioning itself as a leading Chinese supplier of high-end specialty steel and titanium/titanium alloy new materials, with newly disclosed capabilities in powder metallurgy and plasma atomization.

moat_factors.description: Upstream HSS/alloy steel production feeds downstream cutting tools and titanium alloy processing, giving a stated cost advantage over peers who buy raw steel externally.

Long operating history and historically dominant volume share in Chinese HSS gives procurement and customer-relationship advantages ("supply loyalty") that support pricing power during cost inflation.

moat_factors.factor: Technology / IP in powder metallurgy and plasma atomization
moat_factors.description: One of few Chinese firms with plasma atomization powder-making capability for ultra-high-purity titanium alloy powder; proprietary powder metallurgy HSS grades (TPM330, TPMD31); early mover in nuclear fusion materials (TPM304B7 high-boron steel, RAFM steel R&D).

moat_factors.factor: Capital markets access via TG Tech BSE listing
moat_factors.description: First HK-listed red-chip company to spin off a subsidiary onto the Beijing Stock Exchange (May 2025), providing TG Tech with a dedicated funding channel (12 strategic investors including CITIC Securities, Guotai Junan, CICC) for titanium alloy capacity expansion.

Aerospace- and medical-grade material customers require lengthy certification (e.g., ISO13485, AMS4931 standards), creating some switching costs once qualified, but commodity grades of DS/HSS/cutting tools face intense price competition domestically and from imports/exports tariff exposure.

weaknesses: Commodity nature of core DS/HSS steel products exposes margins directly to raw material (alloy/tungsten/molybdenum) price cycles and to Chinese manufacturing PMI cycles

Heavy reliance on a single or few large consumer-electronics end customers for high-margin titanium alloy wire — FY2025 showed a material swing when a major smartphone customer shifted from titanium to aluminum alloy frames in several models
Export segments (cutting tools, HSS, DS) directly exposed to US tariff policy and a sluggish European market, which depressed FY2025 export volumes and margins
Trade receivables and loss allowances have been rising (loss allowance 5.1% of trade and bills receivable in FY2025, up from 4.8%), partly from extending payment terms to European customers
Minority-held structure (TG Tech ~67.6-74% owned) means titanium alloy segment profit is partially diluted to non-controlling interests and subject to separate BSE disclosure/governance dynamics

growth_drivers: Titanium alloy/new materials expansion via TG Tech — BSE listing proceeds earmarked for high-end titanium alloy rod/wire production line expansion targeting aerospace, 3D printing and healthcare
Powder metallurgy and plasma atomization as stated primary growth engines for 2026, enabling higher-value-added HSS and ultra-high-purity titanium alloy powder products

Aerospace material breakthroughs — first deliveries of aerospace-grade titanium alloy wire and fasteners (AMS4931-certified), and nuclear fusion materials (600kg-class TPM304B7 high-boron steel plates, RAFM steel R&D) targeting China's domestic nuclear/aerospace supply chain localization

Expected recovery in consumer electronics titanium demand — management states major end customers resumed mass supply of new (titanium-using) products in Q4 2025/into 2026 after a temporary aluminum-alloy substitution phase
Humanoid robotics and new energy vehicle (NEV) component demand for high-nitrogen alloy and high-precision die steel materials
Overseas production capacity expansion — Thailand precision tools factory ramping capacity to provide a tariff-resilient export base and supply-chain buffer

Selective equity stakes/partnerships (e.g., Shanghai GZclad laser cladding/additive manufacturing, Jiangsu Tiangong Tigiant New Materials for plasma atomization tech, Hengerda New Materials collaboration) to access adjacent new-materials technology and industry consolidation opportunities

business.description: FY2025 titanium alloy revenue fell 17.2% YoY and ASP fell 27% after a key consumer electronics customer substituted aluminum alloy for titanium in most models, showing high sensitivity to a small number of large customers' design decisions.

DS, HSS and cutting tools revenues move with Chinese manufacturing PMI, automotive/NEV die-casting demand, and global machine tool production; FY2022-FY2023 saw revenue declines of ~12% and further softness into FY2024-2025.

US tariffs have already cut HSS export volume by ~50% and depressed cutting tools/DS export pricing in FY2025; further escalation would hit margins given exports are 27-57% of segment revenue depending on product.

business.risk: Rising trade receivables and credit risk
business.description: Trade and bills receivable rose from RMB2,816m to RMB3,207m in FY2025 with loss allowance rising to 5.1%, partly due to extending payment terms to European customers amid weak European demand.

financial.description: Total debt grew from RMB2,895m (FY2023) to RMB4,061m (H1 FY2026), while cash is far lower (~RMB1,325m); net debt position is material relative to ~RMB8.1bn equity.
EUR-denominated export receivables create FX gain/loss volatility (FY2025 benefited from EUR appreciation vs RMB); broader RMB movements affect export competitiveness.
TG Tools has third-party investor redeemable equity interests generating finance costs; redemptions in April 2025 reduced but did not eliminate this liability.

regulatory.description: TG Tech's separate listing creates dual-listing governance complexity, related-party transaction scrutiny, and potential future dilution of the Group's economic interest if TG Tech raises further equity.

Growth narrative is closely tied to Chinese state-directed strategic emerging industries (nuclear fusion, aerospace, humanoid robotics, import substitution); policy shifts could change the investment calculus for these nascent revenue lines.
US and, to a lesser extent, EU trade policy directly affects cutting tools, HSS and DS export revenue and pricing; already a drag in FY2025.

macro.description: Revenue is correlated with Chinese industrial production, automotive and machine tool output; a slowdown in China's ~5% GDP growth trend would directly pressure domestic DS/HSS/cutting tools demand.

Key inputs are molybdenum, chromium, vanadium, tungsten and cobalt alloys and titanium sponge; a June 2026 HSS price increase was explicitly attributed to rising alloy costs. Ability to pass through costs depends on demand conditions, which are cyclical.
Aerospace and nuclear fusion materials are nascent, long-cycle, and investment-dependent; commercialization timelines are uncertain despite early technical breakthroughs.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's special/tool steel output grew modestly (crude steel for tool steel +2.4% in FY2025) with management citing improving prosperity; the global titanium alloy wire market is projected to grow from ~US$6.57bn (2026E) to ~US$11.6bn (2035E), a ~6.5% CAGR, driven by aerospace, medical, 3D printing and consumer electronics. High-tech manufacturing PMI improved through Q4 2025 (50.5 to 52.5), and metal-cutting machine tool production grew 9.7% YoY in 2025, both supportive for cutting tools demand.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high — commodity steel segments (DS, HSS) are closely tied to automotive, machinery and construction-adjacent manufacturing cycles in China and globally; titanium alloy segment cyclicality is driven by consumer electronics product cycles (smartphone design choices) and longer-cycle aerospace/medical adoption.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — the Group carries meaningful debt (~RMB4.1bn at H1 FY2026) plus contingent redeemable equity interests bearing finance costs; declining Chinese deposit rates have also reduced interest income on cash balances.
macro_factors.currency_exposure: EUR exposure via European export receivables (recent EUR appreciation vs RMB was a FY2025 tailwind); USD/RMB indirectly relevant via US tariff policy affecting export competitiveness rather than direct FX translation, since most operations and reporting are RMB-denominated; HKEX listing currency (HKD) vs RMB functional currency for valuation purposes.

recent_developments.event: H1 FY2026 revenue RMB2,471m (+5.5% YoY... note: per Metrics.csv H1 FY2026 revenue RMB2,471.1m vs H1 FY2025 RMB2,342.5m, +5.5%); gross profit RMB613.4m (+38.2% YoY) on a sharp gross margin recovery to 24.8% from 18.9%; net profit attributable to shareholders RMB226.3m (+11.2% YoY).

Group issued a high-speed steel price increase notice, citing continued rises in alloy raw material (tungsten, molybdenum) costs; tungsten demand also cited as a tailwind via PCB drill-bit tungsten rod demand.
Jiangsu Tiangong Technology (TG Tech, 920068.BJ) included in the Beijing Stock Exchange's Specialized and Sophisticated ('little giant') component index.
0826.HK shares hit an intraday all-time high of HK$5.36, with market capitalization approaching HK$14 billion, before retracing to roughly HK$2.9-3.7 range by mid-2026 amid broader volatility.

Jiangsu Tiangong Investment Management (indirect wholly-owned subsidiary) made a further subscription into Shanghai GZclad (laser cladding/additive manufacturing), following a similar September 2025 investment, for a combined ~10.53% stake.
Group gained access to plasma atomization technology (for titanium, high-temperature alloys, copper alloys) via equity interest in Jiangsu Tiangong Tigiant New Materials Co., Ltd.

TG Tech (titanium alloy subsidiary) listed on the Beijing Stock Exchange (code 920068) — first HK-listed red-chip company to spin off a subsidiary onto the BSE; IPO priced at RMB3.94/share, first-day close up 411.93% to RMB20.17, market cap exceeding RMB13 billion at listing; 12 strategic investors including CITIC Securities, Guotai Junan and CICC took a 30% allocation under lock-up.

TG Tech delivered its first aerospace-grade titanium alloy wire/fastener order and signed a joint development agreement with the Aerospace Precision Engineering Research Institute for AMS4931-certified TC4 titanium alloy wire for civil aircraft/UAV fasteners.

Full-year revenue declined 2.3% to RMB4,719m but net profit attributable to shareholders rose 11.5% to RMB400.2m as domestic DS/HSS/cutting tools demand recovered and raw material cost pass-through improved margins, offsetting a 17.2% decline in titanium alloy revenue.

guidance.as_of: FY2025 Annual Report (Chairman's Statement and Outlook), published 30 March 2026

items.target: Powder metallurgy, plasma atomization technology, high-nitrogen alloy materials, and nuclear fusion materials (304B7 high-boron stainless steel, RAFM steel) designated as primary 2026 growth drivers
items.notes: No specific quantitative revenue or margin targets disclosed; qualitative strategic priorities only.

items.target: Management expects the consumer electronics adjustment period to have passed, with major customers initiating mass supply of new (titanium-using) products from Q4 2025
items.notes: No specific revenue figure given; qualitative recovery expectation only.

items.target: Expand market share in key component materials for humanoid robots and nuclear power equipment materials; expand titanium materials and 3D printing powder share in consumer electronics/aerospace
items.notes: No quantified share or revenue targets provided in the filing.

items.target: Continue optimizing global capacity allocation, including continued ramp-up of the Thailand precision tools factory
items.notes: No capex figures disclosed in the annual report text reviewed.

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Zhu Xiaokun characterized FY2025 as a 'bottoming-out and rebound' year, citing successful pass-through of raw material costs via 'absolute pricing power' of high-end products, and framed 2026 around powder metallurgy and plasma atomization as the primary growth engines, with an ambition to become 'a world-leading provider of high-end equipment material solutions.' No specific numeric FY2026 revenue, margin, or EPS guidance was found in the annual report MD&A; guidance is largely qualitative/strategic rather than quantitative targets.

bull_case: Successful BSE spin-off listing of TG Tech (titanium alloy subsidiary) unlocked a dedicated funding channel and a standalone valuation (first-day pop to RMB13bn market cap) that may not be fully reflected in the HK-listed parent's valuation, creating a potential sum-of-the-parts re-rating opportunity

Early-mover technology position in plasma atomization titanium powder and powder metallurgy HSS, with disclosed breakthroughs in nuclear fusion materials (high-boron steel, RAFM steel) and aerospace-grade titanium wire, aligning with China's strategic emerging industries policy push and import-substitution tailwinds

H1 FY2026 results show a sharp margin recovery (gross margin 24.8% vs 18.9% a year earlier) alongside revenue growth, suggesting the FY2025 trough (driven by the titanium/consumer-electronics ASP decline) may have passed

Demonstrated pricing power in domestic DS and HSS during the FY2025 recovery, with the Group able to pass through rising alloy/raw material costs to customers, supporting margin resilience in an upcycle

Diversified end-market exposure (automotive/NEV, humanoid robotics, aerospace, medical, nuclear, consumer electronics) provides multiple avenues for growth beyond the historically commodity-like core steel business
bear_case: High customer/end-market concentration risk demonstrated vividly in FY2025, when a single consumer-electronics customer's design shift away from titanium cut segment revenue by 17% and gross margin by nearly 7 points — the pattern could recur

Commodity DS/HSS/cutting tools segments remain exposed to Chinese manufacturing cyclicality and US/EU tariff and trade-policy risk, which already cut HSS export volumes ~50% and compressed cutting tools export margins in FY2025

Rising leverage (total debt roughly RMB4.1bn at H1 FY2026, up from RMB2.9bn in FY2023) combined with growing trade receivables and loss allowances raises balance sheet and working-capital risk, especially given extended payment terms to stressed European customers

Guidance from management is largely qualitative/strategic (new technology narratives around nuclear fusion, humanoid robotics, plasma atomization) without quantified revenue or margin targets, making it difficult to hold management accountable to specific commitments and raising execution-risk / promotional-narrative concerns

Stock price volatility has been extreme (intraday all-time high of HK$5.36 in February 2026 retracing to roughly HK$2.9-3.7 by mid-2026), suggesting speculative positioning tied to the titanium/new-materials growth story that could unwind if commercialization timelines for nuclear fusion, aerospace, and humanoid robotics materials disappoint
